facts.raw_span: 6-month history of progressive neck pain radiating to his left hand
pain was described as electrical in nature
numbness in the C8–T1 dermatomes
weakness in fine movements and a weak grip of the left hand
marked atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand
muscle strength of 3/5
marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra
extensive paravertebral soft tissue component
lesion was intermediate to low signal on T1-weighted images
lesion was intermediate on T2-weighted images
lesion showed heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
lesion involved the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand, along with the imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, and heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration, is consistent with a chordoma.
The patient's imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, could be consistent with an osteosarcoma.

The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand, along with the imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, could be consistent with a plasmacytoma.
The patient's imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, could be consistent with metastatic disease.

The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand, along with the imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, could be consistent with discitis.
The patient's imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, could be consistent with spondylodiscitis.

The patient's presentation of progressive neck pain radiating to the left hand, along with the imaging findings of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, and extensive paravertebral soft tissue component, could be consistent with a spinal epidural abscess.
The patient's presentation of neck pain radiating to the left hand, along with the symptoms of numbness in the C8-T1 dermatomes, could be consistent with a herniated disc.
It explains the marked atrophy of the hypothenar and interosseous muscles of the left hand, muscle strength of 3/5, and the lesion involved the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments.

rationales.F05: Muscle atrophy is more typical of vertebral tumors than of discitis or spinal epidural abscess.
rationales.F06: Muscle weakness is more typical of vertebral tumors than of discitis or spinal epidural abscess.
rationales.F07: Osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra is highly suggestive of a vertebral tumor.
rationales.F12: Involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments is more typical of vertebral tumors than of discitis or spinal epidural abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: Chordoma is the most specific diagnosis that explains the marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, as well as the patient's progressive neck pain and neurological symptoms, without any strong contradictions.
